Based on RFC2617 (http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2617), the value of
'qop-options' directive should be quoted with double quotes:

```
qop-options
     This directive is optional, but is made so only for backward
     compatibility with RFC 2069 [6]; it SHOULD be used by all
     implementations compliant with this version of the Digest
     scheme. If present, it is a quoted string of one or more
     tokens indicating the "quality of protection" values supported by
     the server.  The value "auth" indicates authentication; the
     value "auth-int" indicates authentication with
     integrity protection; see the
```

curl comamnd-line tool also appends these quotes. You can see this
by `curl -v --digest --user user:passwd http://example.com/digest-auth`.
Unfortunately, some minor server-side implementations seem to be sensitive
on this difference.

123:        noncebit = "%s:%s:%s:%s:%s" % (nonce, ncvalue, cnonce, qop, HA2)

The PR says the `qop` value should be quoted. Looking at RFC 2617, the `qop` directive in the Authorization header (client request) is actually a token, not a quoted string. But the PR description mentions that some server implementations expect it quoted. Let me check what the actual RFC says about the request qop vs response qop-options.

Actually, re-reading the PR and looking more carefully: the PR description quotes the section about `qop-options` in the server's WWW-Authenticate header (which should be quoted). But in the client's Authorization header, the `qop` value is specified as a token (unquoted) per the RFC. However, the PR says curl quotes it and some servers are sensitive to the difference.

Wait, let me re-read. Actually looking at this more carefully - the `qop` in the Authorization request header per RFC 2617 section 3.2.2 is:

```
qop            = "qop" "=" qop-value
qop-value      = "auth" | "auth-int"
```

This is actually supposed to be unquoted (it's a token, not a quoted-string). But the PR says to quote it. Let me check what curl does and look at the actual change expected.

Let me look at what change is expected:

340b245 Merge pull request #1760 from akitada/fix-hangs-on-streaming-uploads
e5b9ae1 Merge pull request #1754 from Lukasa/verb_change

